about: Dom 2026-10-26 (after /physics1 on his iPhone: five ragdolls + a cut, 0.40 ms a frame): the opponent's body is a physics ragdoll (@frankendom/physics, Jolt WASM, package.json) for PRESENTATION only. The 60 Hz sim (src/fight/duel.ts) and Gate 0 never see it, and nothing it does goes back into the sim. src/fight/ragdoll.ts reads every number and name here. `on`: default on; `?<query>=<v1>` (?physics=v1) = today's death and hit behaviour exactly (the chunk is never fetched). `opponents`: the opponent ids that get a ragdoll, each with the body stem it is drawn in on the 65 rig (src/assets/<body>.glb) and its body measure row per rig (`measure`: rig -> a site path the build copies from the package's data/bodies/, fetched with the chunk; the 106 body, data/rig.json files[body], has its own row from Physics Dev (physics 6ab3c99: minotaur-106.measure.json, 1.7225 m); a rig with no row gets no ragdoll and keeps today's death). `bones`: the package's 20 part ids -> the 65-rig bone names; on a 106 body each goes through data/rig.json `bones` (src/fight/rig-bones.ts bone()), the one 65 -> 106 map, never a second copy. `tickHz` / `maxTicksPerFrame`: the fixed physics step in the scene's own accumulator, beside the sim's. `seed`: the physics world's seed (the engine draws nothing; kept for the package's rand()). `loadAfterFirstFrameMs`: the chunk is imported this long after the first frame, so it never competes with the first visit. `hit`: a landed blow (sim event Hit, the opponent the target) -> the part its location strikes, the impulse (N s) along the attacker's facing plus `lift` up, and the package's stagger (rd.stagger, run on `states.stagger`). `motorTuning`: the package's per-role tracking gain and damping multipliers (keys all < role < part id): 2 / 0.25 for the body (Physics Dev's start), 1 / 1 for the neck and head, which were under-damped at 0.25 on the real clips (#56: settled long-axis median 13.3 deg at 2 / 0.25 vs 3.3 at 1 / 1). `solveHinges`: setTargetPose twists the upper arm / thigh about its long axis so the elbow / knee bend plane matches the clip (physics#14; false = the hinge as built). True (2026-10-26, physics a382384 with the left elbow's hinge sign fixed; measured on the 106 Minotaur's real clips, Mac M5, 15 s of fight each, bone direction = local +Y): on, the forearm / hand direction error is 17.3 / 21.7 deg live median (10.1 / 11.0 settled) against 41.9 / 41.8 off; the upper arm's direction is unchanged (16.0 vs 16.1) and its extra full-angle error (38.6 vs 21.1) is roll about the bone, which the stills do not show as a twist on the skin. (#58 had it off: its 'long axis' column used local X, which on these rigs is across the bone, so it counted that roll as direction.) `states`: passed to createPhysics, over the package's data/states.json key by key: `stagger` (Physics Dev's brief: arm 0.9 / forearm 0.6 / hand 0.12, the rest at the torso's 0.6, eased in 0.05 s, held 0.5 s, back over 0.35 s) and `death` (the package's own values: 1 -> 0.01 over 1 s, limp damper 2, sleeps under 0.02 m2/s2 for 4 ticks). `blend`: per part, the share of the ragdoll's pose the bones show at the dip's deepest (the dip's own shape); an unlisted part shows the clip. The spine shows fully, the neck and head half, the arms not yet. On the 106 Minotaur with physics a382384 (2026-10-26: the left-elbow hinge sign fixed, solveHinges on) the forearm and hand follow the clip's direction within 17 / 22 deg live median (10 / 11 settled), but a first try at 0.3 on the arms drew a mid-swing cleaver arm well down from the clip in the stills; the arm share is a follow-up with paired stills. Before that fix the arms were 40-45 deg off and any share flung them. `kill`: the killing blow (sim event Killed): the capsules snap onto the killing frame's pose (rd.snapToTarget), then the part by location takes the impulse along the attacker's facing plus `lift`, the death ramp runs and the bones follow the ragdoll until it sleeps; the corpse stays down until the rematch (rd.reset). `blendInS`: seconds from the clip's pose to the ragdoll's after the kill; 0 since the snap (no pop measured at 0/2/4 ticks). `finisher`: what a ragdolled opponent's kill does with the finisher rotation, `default` unless `?<query>=<a key of values>`. `keep` (?ragdoll=finishers): a cinematic finisher (Split Crown, Decapitation, Run Through, Opened) plays exactly as before and gets no ragdoll; only the plain death (the rotation's no-ceremony outcome, about 1 blade kill in 5, and every kick and skill kill) falls as a ragdoll. `physics` is the DEFAULT since 2026-10-27 (Dom: everything on the main URL; the finishers are physics cuts + ragdoll, ?ragdoll=v1 = the plain death below). `skip` (the default 2026-10-26 to 2026-10-27, Dom: let's get this always on; ?ragdoll=v1 or ?ragdoll=always): every death of his is the plain death and falls as a ragdoll; the finisher (picture and its death cue) is skipped for that kill.

cut.about: M5 cuts (physics f38dba0, docs/API.md 'Cuts (M5)'), PRESENTATION ONLY like the rest of this file (the sim and Gate 0 never see a cut; ?physics=v1 = no ragdoll, so no cut and no tap). `on`: false = no cut at all. `log`: the page's list of sim-side-presentation cut events ({ type: 'cut', unit, gear, source }), read by Strategy's loot screen later (globalThis[log]; one fight's cuts, emptied on the rematch). `onKill`: the sim's Killed.location -> the unit that leaves with that killing blow (a head-zone kill takes the head). `sever`: the unit V1's decapitation finisher takes (?ragdoll=finishers: V1's flying head stays the picture; the package's cut is made too, for its event and gear). `kill`: that cut's push, along the killing blow's facing (impulse N s, lift up). `tap`: the corpse tap (the butcher's table): a tap (no more than maxMovePx of drag and maxMs long, so the camera drag never cuts) on the corpse once the ragdoll is `needs` (frozen) raycasts the skinned body, takes the heaviest bone of the face it meets, and cuts the first unit of `order` whose bone it hangs under (the package's cut_role bones: head, an arm, a leg, then the torso at the waist, which carries everything above); `impulse` / `lift`: the piece's push along the tap's ray. `seam`: how the skinned body is split (src/fight/cut-pieces.ts): a triangle goes with the piece when the carried bones hold at least `piece` of its weight (the rule characters.ts sever() bakes the finisher's head with), and stays on the body only when no vertex of it has `bodyKeepBelow` of its weight carried (a triangle across the cut belongs to neither: the cap covers the seam). `cap`: the two stump caps (plain balls until Physics Dev's real cut-piece meshes land) (the body's, on the parent part, and the piece's, on the severed part): colour, and radiusMult times the cut part's capsule radius. `helmet`: the rigid helmet prop's placeholder mesh (only an opponent row with helmet: true gets one; the Minotaur wears none, no armour until beta). The world steps while the package's `rd.awake` says a body of the ragdoll is awake (a frozen corpse is not; the piece a cut wakes is): physics 4c708f7 replaced the page's `settleS` timer. The package's three-rig applyPose places every cut bone on its capsule's joint.

strike.about: Dom 2026-10-28 (phone: the hint said Strike to dismember and nothing cut): once a corpse is frozen (cut.tap.needs), ANY attack press (STRIKE, heavy, stab, kick, a spell, the keys, a mouse click) while the hero stands within nearM metres of it cuts a part: the one under the pointer when the press carries a point that strikes a unit still on the body (a click or a tap on a part), else the NEXT unit of cut.tap.order still on it, so a player who never aims still dismembers the whole body. A tap on the canvas that misses the body does the same inside nearM. Presentation only: the sim never sees it.

cue.about: Dom 2026-10-28 (phone: the yellow circles with text look tacky): HIDDEN by default (`default` false); ?cues=v1 (`query`/`v1`) brings them back; the plain tap on a body part still cuts. Original ruling, Dom 2026-10-27 (phone test: no head came off, he did not know where to tap): once the corpse is frozen (cut.tap.needs) for delayS seconds, a pulsing round button labelled by `labels` sits on each unit of `units` that is still on it (a unit's cut bone on screen); a tap on it cuts that unit (the same push as a corpse tap). Presentation only, nothing is sent to the sim.

corpse.about: Strategy's live-zone brief (2026-10-27): a dead foe's body stays where it fell while the zone respawns him (ragdoll.ts leaveCorpse, called by the zone loop at the respawn). `keepSeconds`: how long the whole copy stands (V1: clientRespawn 90 s, frankendom-main preview-rules-defs.json). `pieceSeconds`: how long the pieces that were cut off it stay (V1: feel-rules.json cut piece 12 s). `max`: how many corpses stand at once, the oldest dropped first (V1 campMax 4). A corpse is a frozen copy of the rig as it lies (nothing animates it); presentation only. M8 (2026-10-27): a corpse of a body with the cut GLB (the Minotaur) KEEPS ITS OWN RAGDOLL (`cuttable`: the old rd, frozen, with its own cut rig on the cloned scene), so the cut buttons (cut.cue) and a tap work on it again and the piece it loses flies; a body without the cut GLB stays a static copy. Each ragdoll the world holds (the live foe and every cuttable corpse) has its own lane in the one Jolt world, `slotSpacingM` metres apart along x (ragdolls of different groups collide, and every sim frame is the foe's group frame, so the live foe's respawn would otherwise stand inside the corpse); max + 1 lanes. `event`: the bus name (feel.on) every cut is announced under, payload { unit, gear, source, corpseId } (read-only info for V3's loot and zone code; the fight's outcome never reads it); corpseId is `<opponent id>#<life>`, the same for the live foe's kill cut and every later cut of his corpse.

finisherCuts.about: Strategy's ruling (2026-10-26): V3's finishers become PHYSICS cuts + ragdoll, keeping V1's camera, blood and sound timing rows (the kill cam stays). They play under ?ragdoll=finishers (finisher mode 'physics'): the rotation picks as in V1, the scene plays the finisher's own camera, blood and sound by its id from src/fight/finisher-defs.json, and the victim's body is the ragdoll with the cut below instead of V1's victim clip. The default (finisher 'skip') is unchanged: every death the plain ragdoll death. ?ragdoll=clips = V1's cinematic finishers with V1's victim clips and no ragdoll (the old 'keep'); ?physics=v1 = V1 as it was. PRESENTATION ONLY (the sim and Gate 0 never see it). `rows`: one per finisher id of finisher-defs.json that has a physics body (a finisher with no row, such as Hamstrung and Execution, keeps its clips). `unit`: the package's cut unit (head, arm_left, arm_right, leg_left, leg_right, torso_waist) that leaves the body, or null = no cut (the blade stays through the body). `atS`: seconds after the killing blow the cut is made (0 = with the kill, as the head-zone kill's). `push`: a multiplier on kill.impulse (0.25 = the body sags and the stuck blade holds it up). `kill`: the cut piece's push {impulse, lift}, null = cut.kill. The camera, blood and sound are the finisher's own rows in finisher-defs.json, by the same id (nothing here re-states them: the kill cam is V1's, unchanged). `plane`: what V1's finisher does that the unit only stands in for (null = the unit is the cut), for Strategy to rule on a new cut plane.

splitCrown.plane: M9a (physics 9056ef7): the head leaves with the sagittal cut (the cut GLB's piece_head_left / piece_head_right, cap_split_* faces, unit head_split) but head_split is VISUAL-ONLY: both halves follow the one head capsule and fly as one piece (independent halves are the package's step 2), and the cut stops at the neck (V1's Split Crown cleaves down to the chest). A body whose cut GLB has no head_split gets the plain head cut (the stand-in).

runThrough.plane: Dom 2026-10-27: the blade stays through him (push 0.25) and the body now also shows the package's belly wound decal (visual-only) where its cut GLB carries belly_open, with the finisher's own chest-entry and back-exit blood; a body without it shows blood only.

dismember.plane: Dom 2026-10-27 (V1 dismemberment): the right arm leaves with the kill, the left arm and a leg 0.35 s later (two blows); each is a package cut.

hamstringCut.plane: Dom 2026-10-27 (V1 hamstring): both legs cut low, the second 0.3 s after the first, so he drops; V1's is two knee blows and a back stab, the unit is a leg cut, not the knee.

opened.plane: M9a (physics 9056ef7): the belly opens as the cut GLB's wound decal (cap_belly_opening, unit belly_open, VISUAL-ONLY: no hole in the torso skin, no spilled guts, the body stays whole); V1's Opened spills the guts with the halves held by the spine. A body whose cut GLB has no belly_open gets torso_waist (the whole trunk severed at the waist, V1's baked waist cut), the earlier stand-in.
